row.team_price_text: Small Business: no public price (demo / sales)
row.evidence: Stonly's API guide says SCIM can create, update and deactivate users and groups but must be enabled by contacting Stonly support and only officially supports Okta; the pricing page publishes no prices and lists SSO only on the custom Enterprise plan.
row.notes: New in 2026-09. Quote-only: the pricing page shows Small Business (5 team members, under 100 employees) and Enterprise (custom) with no public price on either; the only route is 'See Stonly in action' or 'Schedule a call'. SCIM is documented (SCIM 2.0 under /api/v3/scim, Basic auth with the team API key) but has to be switched on by Stonly support, and no plan is named for it. SSO (SAML 2.0) is an add-on on the Enterprise plan. The SCIM guide says only Okta is officially supported (set up as the generic 'SCIM 2.0 Test App (Header Auth)'), which would make it partial if prices were public; the OpenAPI tag also mentions Azure AD (see conflicts). Stonly also has a non-SCIM provisioning REST API (users, groups, team access) with the same API key, rate limited to 200 requests per hour per endpoint per IP. Plan for the API key is not stated. Category: support knowledge base / guides.

plans.name: Basic
plans.notes: Not sold; accounts fall back to Basic after the 14-day Small Business trial. 1 team member, 400 guide views/mo.

plans.name: Small Business
plans.price_text: No public price ('See Stonly in action')
plans.notes: 5 team members, 4,000 guide views, for companies under 100 employees. SSO is listed under Enterprise only.

plans.name: Enterprise
plans.notes: SSO is an add-on on Enterprise. SCIM plan is not stated; SCIM is enabled on request by Stonly support.

auth.token_source: Team Management > Integrations > API key (sent as Basic base64(':apiKey'))

filtering.notes: Single-attribute eq filter only; complex filters return 400 invalidFilter. Filterable attribute names are not listed.

roles.how: SCIM User schema has a roles array (string or {value, display, type, primary}); team role is Member or Admin

rate_limits.text: 200 requests per hour per endpoint per IP address (public API)

limitations.text: Only Okta is officially supported, via Okta's generic SCIM 2.0 Test App (Header Auth); there is no Stonly app in the Okta catalogue.
SCIM must be enabled by Stonly support.
Only single-attribute eq filters are supported.

scim.notes: plan=Enterprise is inferred under the quote-only rule (no public prices; SCIM enabled via Stonly support), not stated by Stonly. The OpenAPI spec lists the SCIM paths under https://public.stonly.com/api/v3 (EU) or https://public.us.stonly.com/api/v3 (US); the Okta guide uses https://api.stonly.com/api/v3/scim.

capabilities.notes: delete_user = remove the user from the team (DELETE /team/access).

rate_limits.text: 200 requests per hour per endpoint per IP address

user_api.notes: Plan for API access is not stated on the pricing page or in the API guide. US-hosted teams use https://public.us.stonly.com/api/v3.

okta.notes: No Stonly app in the OIN (okta.com/integrations/stonly/ 404); Stonly documents Okta's generic 'SCIM 2.0 Test App (Header Auth)'. SAML SSO with Okta is supported per the SSO guide.

fallbacks.notes: SSO guide says team members can be provisioned from the IdP instead of email invitations, but does not say whether this is JIT on SAML sign-in or SCIM.

conflicts.text: The help-centre SCIM guide says the SCIM API 'only officially supports Okta', while the OpenAPI tag describes the SCIM endpoints as for 'Okta, Azure AD, ...'. Behaviour taken from the help-centre guide.
The Okta guide gives the SCIM base URL as https://api.stonly.com/api/v3/scim, while the OpenAPI spec's servers are https://public.stonly.com/api/v3 (EU) and https://public.us.stonly.com/api/v3 (US).

open_questions: Which plan includes SCIM, and whether it costs extra, is not published; Stonly says to contact support.
Whether SCIM deactivation frees the seat or ends active sessions is not documented.
Whether the SCIM endpoint is supported with Entra ID or other IdPs (the spec mentions Azure AD, the guide says Okta only).
Whether any audit-log API or user-event webhooks exist is not documented.
Which plans include the public API key is not stated.
